definition.name: NXspm_piezoelectric_material
definition.doc: Description and properties of the piezoelectric actuator materials. The piezoelectric actuator is usually composed of polycrystalline solids and attached at the head of the tip or cantilever. The material deforms when the external electric field (e.g., electric force) is applied.

field.name: name
field.doc: The name of the material of the piezo scanner such as lead zirconate titanate (PZT).

field.name: identifierNAME
field.doc:
A persistent identifier of the piezo material. NAME and the ``@type`` attribute name the authority that issued the identifier (e.g. ``identifier_cas`` with ``@type`` = ``CAS``).
Molecular identifiers such as InChI are not suitable, since piezoelectric ceramics and solid solutions are not discrete molecules.

attribute.name: type
attribute.doc: The authority that issued the identifier.

item.doc: CAS Registry Number, assigned by the Chemical Abstracts Service to chemical substances, including inorganic compounds and solid solutions, in the format ``NNNNNNN-NN-N`` (e.g. ``12626-81-2`` for lead zirconate titanate). Suitable for any piezo material, independent of its crystal structure.

Entry number in the Crystallography Open Database (https://www.crystallography.net), an open-access collection of crystal structures. Identifies a specific crystal structure, e.g. of a single crystal or of the crystalline phase of a ceramic.
Collection code in the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database, a curated (licensed) database of inorganic crystal structures.
Identifier in the Materials Project (``mp-`` followed by a number, https://materialsproject.org), a database of computed material properties.

field.name: type
field.doc: The type of the material of the piezo scanner.

item.doc: Polycrystalline piezoelectric ceramic, e.g. lead zirconate titanate (PZT) or barium titanate. Most common material of SPM piezo scanners.
Piezoelectric single crystal, e.g. quartz, lithium niobate, or PMN-PT.
Piezoelectric polymer film, e.g. polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF).
Composite of a piezoelectric ceramic and a polymer matrix.
Deposited piezoelectric thin film, e.g. aluminium nitride or zinc oxide.

field.name: density
field.doc: The density of the piezo material.

field.name: relative_permittivity
field.doc: The relative permittivity (dielectric constant) of the piezo material.

field.name: D_piezoelectric_constant
field.doc: The piezoelectric charge coefficient :math:`d_{ij}` of the material, which relates the electric polarization generated to the applied mechanical stress. The capitalized part ``D`` is replaced by the coefficient name, e.g. ``d33_piezoelectric_constant`` or ``d31_piezoelectric_constant``.

field.name: G_voltage_constant
field.doc: The piezoelectric voltage coefficient :math:`g_{ij}` of the material, which relates the electric field produced to the applied mechanical stress. The capitalized part ``G`` is replaced by the coefficient name, e.g. ``g33_voltage_constant`` or ``g31_voltage_constant``, analogous to :ref:`D_piezoelectric_constant </NXspm_piezoelectric_material/D_piezoelectric_constant-field>`.

field.name: K_electromechanical_constant
field.doc: The electromechanical constant measures the efficiency of the conversion of mechanical energy into electrical energy.

field.name: P_pyroelectric_constant
field.doc: The pyroelectric constant defines the change of the polarization vector of the piezoelectric material per unit change in temperature.

field.name: acoustic_impedance
field.doc: The acoustic impedance of the piezo material.

field.name: young_modulus
field.doc: The Young's modulus of the piezo material.

field.name: surface_resistivity
field.doc: The surface resistivity of the piezo material.

field.name: temperature_range
field.doc: The operating temperature range of the piezo material, i.e. the range of temperatures in which the piezoelectric component is specified to work, given as [min, max].

field.name: glass_transition_temperature
field.doc: The range of temperature where a piezoelectric hard material transforms into the viscous state.
